cands.bio: San Francisco Supervisor for District 1 since January 2021 and Budget Committee chair since 2023. Earlier worked as an aide to Supervisors Sophie Maxwell and Aaron Peskin and to District Attorney Kamala Harris, and held roles at Recreation and Parks and City College of San Francisco.

endorsements.text: Nancy Pelosi (endorsed May 18, 2026), Sen. Adam Schiff, Reps. Judy Chu, Zoe Lofgren, Julia Brownley and Norma Torres, and the California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, National Nurses United, SEIU California and the San Francisco Labor Council.
Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi endorsed Chan for Congress.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Chan's positions on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, gun laws, or school vouchers and charters. We found no recorded Board votes of hers on police pensions or pay. The campaign website page was cut off partway through, so some of her policy pages and her later record as supervisor were not read. We found no controversies about her that were documented in the pages we read.

qual.background: Elected San Francisco Supervisor in 2020 and re-elected in 2024; Budget Committee chair since 2023. Earlier a legislative aide to two supervisors, a public safety and communications aide to District Attorney Kamala Harris, and a representative for then-Assemblymember Kevin Mullin.
qual.why: Nearly six years in local elected office, including chairing the committee that handles a roughly $14.6 billion city budget, plus earlier legislative staff work. She has no state or federal legislative service.
qual.label: Nearly six years in local elected office, including chairing the committee that handles a roughly $14.6 billion city budget, plus earlier legislative staff work. She has no state or federal legislative service.

workers-first.evidence: Says she supports a pathway to citizenship, protecting San Francisco as a sanctuary city, and an end to ICE raids and what she calls abuses by ICE and CBP.

pro-life.evidence: Says she will fight for access to the full range of reproductive health care including abortion, and will push to restore full funding for Planned Parenthood.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Voted in 2021 as a supervisor, in an 8–3 Board vote, to block a 495-unit apartment project (one-quarter affordable) on a Nordstrom valet lot next to a BART station, saying she supported 'the right housing in the right places.'

back-police-order.evidence: Opposed the 2022 recall of District Attorney Chesa Boudin, though 57% of her own District 1 voted for the recall.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 4 priorities; 2 backed by their record, 0 only promised

roots.summary: Born in Hong Kong, she moved to San Francisco at age 13, attended Galileo High School and UC Davis, and has worked in San Francisco city politics and government since.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: With Supervisor Peskin, asked the city attorney to sue the state over SB 423's streamlined housing approvals, arguing the law unfairly targeted San Francisco, which she said had produced enough market-rate housing. She also sponsored legislation to streamline approvals for 100% affordable projects.

cands.bio: California state senator for San Francisco since 2016 and former San Francisco supervisor (2011–2016). Attorney who clerked for the New Jersey Supreme Court and worked as a San Francisco deputy city attorney. Chairs the Senate Budget and Fiscal Review Committee. Duke and Harvard Law graduate.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in the 2026 race by California Attorney General Rob Bonta, San Francisco Supervisor Rafael Mandelman, the California Democratic Party, Reps. Ami Bera, Laura Friedman, Josh Harder, Sam Liccardo and Scott Peters, former Mayor London Breed, SEIU California State Council, Nor Cal Carpenters Union, IUOE Local 3, Equality California, YIMBY Action, California Environmental Voters, J Street, and the San Francisco Chronicle Editorial Board.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B visas, police pay and pensions, gun laws, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. The Wikipedia article was cut off partway through the state Senate housing section, and Ballotpedia's 2014 campaign themes and sponsored-bill table were empty or cut off, so any items in those sections are missing. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, and the sources we read contain no direct statements from him on most of the topics above.

qual.label: He has about 15 years in elected legislative office, including budget leadership, plus a legal career with city government, which fits the lawmaking, oversight and budgeting work of the job.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign website says he supports abolishing ICE, making DACA recipients citizens and creating a pathway to citizenship for immigrant communities.

clean-money.evidence: His campaign website says he is neither seeking nor accepting support from AIPAC, citing significant policy differences.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Authored SB 35 (2017), which requires cities that have fallen behind on state housing production goals to streamline approval of new housing.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: Born in Philadelphia and raised in southern New Jersey, he moved to San Francisco in 1997 and has lived in the Castro neighborhood since then, about 29 years.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Describing the 2026 race, Axios San Francisco wrote that 'Wiener often argues for building more housing and embracing politically difficult compromises to deliver results.' Wikipedia also describes him as a prominent advocate for measures to facilitate more housing construction in California.
On SB 35 he said: 'Local control is about how a community achieves its housing goals, not whether it achieves those goals.'
